disposition_reason: ICP-MS results for twelve elements in 87 samples of 21 Polish fruit species are tabulated by fruit group (min, mean, SD, max, P95) on a wet-weight basis.

study.design: Field survey of 21 locally grown fruit species from arable soils in four regions of southern Poland, with soil fractionation, bioconcentration and health risk assessment
study.origin: Opolskie, Śląskie, Małopolskie and Świętokrzyskie regions, southern Poland (locally produced only)
study.market: directly from farmers or local fresh food markets
study.method: HNO3/H2O2 block digestion (130 °C); ICP-MS (USEPA 6020B), cross-checked by ICP-OES
study.qa: CRM BCR-679 white cabbage, recoveries 83-124% for most elements; blanks and duplicates

unresolved: Results are reported only by fruit group (berry, pome, stone, shell); no per-species values are printed, so single species such as blueberry or apple cannot be separated.
Means in Table 3 differ from the group means in the Results text for many element-group pairs; Table 3 values recorded and flagged.
Table 3 prints SDs that are small relative to means and maxima (e.g. Pb stone fruit SD 0.020 vs max 2.069); they may be standard errors; recorded as printed.
Detection rates across all fruits (Cd 57.5%, Pb 58.8%, etc.) are not findings.
